title: Signed Ohm-law current
description: Find the signed current through an ideal ohmic resistor from its applied DC voltage.
assumptions: Linear, constant positive resistance; no temperature, noise, parasitics or semiconductor behavior.
Voltage polarity and positive current direction follow the passive sign convention.
Numerical envelope: abs(V) <= 1e6 V and 1e-9 <= R <= 1e12 ohm; these are computation bounds, not component ratings.

references.title: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 2, 9.4 Ohm's Law

title: Loaded Wheatstone bridge and common-mode voltage
description: Calculate the exact differential output and actual midpoint/common-mode voltages of an unbalanced resistive bridge with a finite detector resistance across its midpoints.
formula: Va0 = Vs R2/(R1+R2); Vb0 = Vs R4/(R3+R4); Ra = R1||R2; Rb = R3||R4; Id = (Va0-Vb0)/(Ra+Rb+Rd); Va = Va0-Id Ra; Vb = Vb0+Id Rb; Vdiff = Id Rd; Vcm = (Va+Vb)/2
assumptions: R1 is excitation-to-left, R2 left-to-ground, R3 excitation-to-right, R4 right-to-ground; the excitation source is ideal.
Detector resistance connects only between left and right midpoints; it has no ground/common-mode loading or bias current.
Detector current is positive left-to-right; differential voltage is left minus right; balanced and negatively unbalanced bridges are supported without division by the open-circuit voltage.
This is an exact linear DC network solution, not a strain/temperature transducer model; no resistor noise, lead resistance or self-heating is modeled.
All five resistances are 1e-9 to 1e12 ohm and abs(Vs) <= 1e6 V; very close balance can incur floating-point cancellation.

references.title: William & Mary, Analog Electronics Chapter 2: Kirchhoff's Laws and Thevenin's Theorem, bridge exercises and Thevenin load relation
University of Colorado Boulder, PHYS 3330 Lab 2, section 2.7 divider Thevenin equivalents

Loaded right midpoint relative to ground

constraints.message: Bridge arms and finite detector resistance must all be positive.
